etymology.historical_story: Fletcher entered Middle English from Anglo-French flecher, associated with fleche, meaning an arrow. Merriam-Webster dates its recorded English use to the fourteenth century. Like Baker and Carpenter, an occupational label also became a surname. Modern readers may therefore encounter Fletcher as a person's name without any implication that the person actually makes arrows. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fletcher)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 fletch 与箭尾羽连在一起，再用英语职业后缀 -er 联想从业者：fletcher 是制箭匠；这是记忆分析，不替代历史词源。

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: 若是姓氏，保留大写 Fletcher，并依本人称谓使用 Encik、Puan、Dr 或其他适当头衔；不要因姓氏来源而把当事人称为制箭匠。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 职业义适合英语历史、传统工艺和射箭材料的讨论。面向普通马来语读者，首次出现时解释为 tukang pembuat anak panah；人名则保留原拼写。
